source.title: Rethinking Circuit Evaluation: Do Circuits Explain Model Errors?
source.authors: Li Zhang; Chu-Qin Geng; Mark Zhang; Chen Yang; Lu-Ke Zhang; Hao-Lin Ye; Xu-Jie Si

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates the GPT-2 small IOI reference circuit and reports that it agrees with the model on many correct prompts but reproduces relatively few of the model’s exact errors. It also shows that the result depends on ablation and evaluation settings.
record.gate_note: The study tests the published IOI manual reference circuit and several extraction methods on GPT-2 small. It does not test backup-head takeover by ablating primary Name Movers, compare circuit overlap or roles across models, or establish that different circuit-finding methods recover the same head classes. IOI results are aggregated over 15 template families and ABBA/BABA order, not reported separately by template or order. Docstring and MIB results do not bear on this GPT-2 small IOI claim.
record.test_reason: The study re-evaluates the published 26-head GPT-2 small IOI circuit under mean, resample and optimal ablation. It reports task faithfulness alongside exact agreement on model-correct and model-error prompts, and shows the circuit reproduces few of the model's errors. It also restores omitted heads and traces how they cause the errors. These are results bearing on V1's completeness and on V5's claims of evaluation sensitivity and partial explanation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that tested circuits reproduce correct predictions far better than the model's particular errors, and recommend exact wrong-answer reproduction as a necessary but not sufficient test. Add that the IOI case study recovers errors by restoring omitted heads: 14.2% to 75.1% held-out, with a 0.41 pp drop in Aok. The authors limit the mechanism traces to this one circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the published GPT-2 small IOI reference circuit and mean knockouts, but evaluates exact agreement with the model’s choices on correct and error strata, alongside other ablations and a recovery extension. It does not reproduce the original study’s full faithfulness, completeness, and minimality analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Exact agreement varies with ablation: the manual IOI circuit’s error agreement is reported as 15.2% under mean ablation, 40.6% under ABC resampling, and 10.0% under optimal ablation. Margin matching changes agreement levels but leaves positive gaps across the IOI configurations. Error reweighting and error-enriched discovery improve error agreement while lowering correct agreement. The targeted extension has different agreement values under mean and resample ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: On Docstring and six MIB settings (Llama-3.1 8B, Gemma-2 2B, Qwen-2.5 0.5B), circuits likewise preserve correct choices better than they reproduce errors. Docstring EAP-IG is an exception, with a negative gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuit explanations generally reproduce model successes better than the model's exact errors.

record.problems: The IOI evaluation pools template families and name orders rather than reporting them separately. The detailed recovery case study concerns one reference circuit and selected errors; the authors state that it does not establish generalization to other circuits or tasks. Some Table 1 confidence-interval alignment is unclear in the flattened text.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded Docstring and MIB circuit evaluations because they do not test the GPT-2 small IOI claim. Also excluded the fresh 5,200-prompt extension check from Table 4 because the text reports only a 0.85-point correct-agreement drop and no exact error-agreement value; it is noted in the paper as exceeding the original 0.5-point tolerance.

untested.parts: Individual head-class roles, and the original completeness and minimality tests, are not re-run.
All of V2. Backup Name Movers are only described; no takeover experiment ablates the primary Name Movers.
All of V3. The MIB and Docstring results concern other tasks and models without IOI head classes.
All of V4. ACDC, EAP-IG and Edge Pruning circuits are compared only on agreement metrics, not on overlap or head classes.
All of V6. Results are pooled over 15 templates × ABBA/BABA, with no per-variant or more-name results.

missing.what: Margin-matched agreement for the ACDC, EAP-IG and Edge Pruning IOI circuits; only the manual-circuit rows are recorded.
Error-conditioned mean and resample replacements, and scalar/threshold calibration, on IOI. The text gives only qualitative results: they raise Aerr, and a subject-logit shift matches them.

record.verdict_notes: The reader misaligned Table 1: the bracketed CI column is 100∆ (the gap), not Aok, so its Aok/CI notes are wrong although the recorded values are right. The reader's V1 'challenges' is too strong: faithfulness as defined in the original holds, and the error-reproduction shortfall is a new criterion, so I give it limits_scope. V6 links were dropped because prompts are pooled. r19–r20 are controls for the study's own extension. r26 duplicates r22.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures exact model-choice agreement and normalized task faithfulness, but does not revalidate each of the 26 heads’ stated functional roles or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria individually.
No experiment ablates the primary Name Movers to test whether backup heads take over.
No test of the same IOI head classes and roles across other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
The study compares circuit outcomes across discovery methods and ablations, but does not test whether those methods recover essentially the same circuit structure.
The study tests multiple ablations, metrics, and prompt/discovery choices, but does not exhaust possible evaluation choices.

IOI evaluations pool 15 template families and ABBA/BABA order; results are not separated by template or order. The study does not test prompts with more names or establish that head roles are identical across variants.
